title: A room booking that changed
text:
The North Street library accepts room bookings up to fourteen days ahead. A booking is confirmed only after the applicant receives an email. Rooms are free for local study groups, but commercial events must pay a fee.

Lena requested a room for Wednesday evening. On Monday she received an email offering Thursday instead, because maintenance would close the building on Wednesday. Her group could not attend on Thursday. She replied that she would prefer to meet the following Wednesday.

The librarian asked Lena to submit a new request rather than change the old email. The original request would be cancelled without charge. Lena told her group not to travel until a new confirmation arrived.
question: Why should the group wait before travelling?
answer: A new confirmation has not arrived.
wrong: Commercial groups never pay a fee.
The library cannot accept future bookings.
evidence: Lena told her group not to travel until a new confirmation arrived.

title: An induction before the first shift
text:
Community Kitchen welcomes new volunteers on Saturday mornings. Volunteers may prepare vegetables after an induction, but only trained staff may operate the large ovens. Closed shoes are required in the kitchen.

Sam had already volunteered at another food project. He expected to begin cooking immediately, but the coordinator explained that every new volunteer must attend this kitchen's induction. Previous experience did not remove that requirement.

Sam's induction was scheduled for ten. His bus arrived at ten fifteen, so he could not join the safety briefing. The coordinator offered him a place the next Saturday. He was welcome to help distribute leaflets outdoors that day, but he could not work in the kitchen until the briefing was complete.
question: What can Sam do before completing the induction?
answer: Help distribute leaflets outdoors.
wrong: Operate the large ovens.
Prepare vegetables in the kitchen.
evidence: He was welcome to help distribute leaflets outdoors that day, but he could not work in the kitchen until the briefing was complete.

title: The delivery window
text:
Westford Furniture gives customers a four-hour delivery window two days before delivery. Drivers call when they are approximately twenty minutes away. The service includes carrying furniture to a room on the ground floor. Upper-floor delivery must be arranged separately.

Nora ordered a desk for her upstairs office. When she read the confirmation, she realised that she had selected standard delivery. She contacted the company before the delivery date. An upstairs service was available for an additional fee, provided that the staircase was wide enough.

Nora sent measurements of the staircase. Staff confirmed that the desk could be carried upstairs and added the service to her order. They also reminded her that the driver's call would not narrow the original delivery window in advance. She still needed someone at home for the whole window.
question: Why does Nora send staircase measurements?
answer: To check whether upstairs delivery is possible.
wrong: To choose an earlier four-hour window.
To cancel the desk order.
evidence: An upstairs service was available for an additional fee, provided that the staircase was wide enough.

title: Joining an evening course
text:
The evening photography course runs for eight Tuesdays. The advertised price covers tuition and access to the classroom. Students must bring a camera or reserve a loan camera before the first lesson. Loan cameras are limited and are allocated in the order requests arrive.

Aisha enrolled online and assumed that a camera would be waiting for her. A reminder email explained the separate reservation process. By the time she requested a loan, all cameras had been allocated.

The tutor suggested that Aisha use a phone for the first two lessons, which focused on composition. Later lessons required a camera with manual controls. Aisha could borrow one from a friend, transfer to the next course, or withdraw before the refund deadline. She chose to borrow one and checked that its controls met the requirements.
question: Why can Aisha use a phone for the first two lessons?
answer: Those lessons focus on composition.
wrong: Phones meet every later requirement.
Her enrolment automatically reserved a camera.
evidence: The tutor suggested that Aisha use a phone for the first two lessons, which focused on composition.

title: A repair estimate
text:
Bright Repairs charges an inspection fee before giving a repair estimate. The fee is deducted from the final bill if the customer authorises the repair. If the customer decides not to proceed, the inspection fee is still payable.

Owen left his laptop for inspection and requested an email estimate. The technician found two faults. Replacing the battery would solve the charging problem, but it would not repair the damaged screen. The estimate listed the two jobs separately.

Owen approved the battery replacement only. The technician recorded that decision and ordered the battery. A notice on the collection desk explained that verbal requests for extra work would not be accepted without a revised authorisation. When Owen collected the laptop, the charging problem was fixed and the screen damage remained, as he had agreed.
question: Which repair did Owen authorise?
answer: The battery replacement only.
wrong: Both the battery and the screen.
The screen replacement only.
evidence: Owen approved the battery replacement only.

title: A flexible work trial
text:
A design company will trial flexible starting times for six weeks. Staff may start between seven thirty and nine thirty, but they must attend scheduled team meetings. The total weekly hours will not change.

Priya wanted to start early so that she could collect her child from school. Her team met at nine on Wednesdays. Her manager approved an early start but explained that the trial did not allow staff to leave a required meeting halfway through.

During the trial, the company would record missed handovers, response times and staff comments. It would compare these with the previous six weeks before deciding whether to keep the arrangement. The announcement promised a review, rather than a permanent entitlement. Priya arranged cover for Wednesday afternoons instead of assuming that the new timetable would solve every scheduling problem.
question: What remains unchanged during the trial?
answer: The total weekly working hours.
wrong: Everyone's starting time.
The arrangement is already permanent.
evidence: The total weekly hours will not change.

title: An accessible route to the museum
text:
The museum's main entrance has twelve steps. A step-free entrance is available on Garden Lane, beside the cafe. Visitors using that entrance should ring the bell, because the door is not left unlocked.

A temporary exhibition is on the second floor. The lift will be closed for maintenance on Monday morning. The permanent ground-floor galleries will remain open, and visitors may use the cafe without buying an exhibition ticket.

Daniel planned a Monday visit with his father, who uses a wheelchair. He telephoned to ask when maintenance would finish. Staff could not promise an exact time, so they offered to move the exhibition tickets to Tuesday. Daniel accepted. He understood that a step-free entrance would allow access to the building but would not, by itself, guarantee access to every floor during maintenance.
question: Why does Daniel move the exhibition visit to Tuesday?
answer: The lift may be unavailable on Monday morning.
wrong: The ground-floor galleries close every Monday.
The cafe requires an exhibition ticket.
evidence: The lift will be closed for maintenance on Monday morning.

title: A deposit for a community hall
text:
River Hall asks for a deposit to hold an event date. The deposit is part of the hire price, not an additional charge. A separate damage bond is payable one week before the event and is returned after inspection if no damage is found.

The neighbourhood group paid the deposit for a Sunday lunch. The organiser later asked whether tables, cleaning and kitchen use were included. The manager confirmed that tables were included, cleaning cost extra and kitchen use required a separate agreement.

The group chose to bring cold food and clean the hall themselves. They signed a checklist showing the furniture provided and the condition of the room. The manager explained that returning the damage bond would not refund the hire price. The organiser circulated the final cost to the group so that members would not confuse the deposit, bond and optional services.
question: What is the deposit used for?
answer: To hold the event date as part of the hire price.
wrong: To pay a refundable damage bond only.
To include every optional service automatically.
evidence: The deposit is part of the hire price, not an additional charge.

title: A health appointment reminder
text:
The clinic sends appointment reminders by text message. Patients should contact reception if they need to change an appointment. Replying to the reminder does not notify the booking team, because the number cannot receive replies.

Marta received a reminder while travelling. She replied that she would be late and assumed that the clinic had changed her time. When she arrived, reception explained that no reply had been received and the appointment had passed.

A nurse checked whether Marta needed urgent assistance. Her visit could safely be rearranged, and the receptionist offered an appointment the next morning. Marta saved the clinic's telephone number and checked the directions. The clinic also reviewed the reminder wording: the instruction to call was present, but staff agreed to put it nearer the start of the message.
question: Why did Marta's reply fail to change the appointment?
answer: The reminder number cannot receive replies.
wrong: Patients are never allowed to change appointments.
The receptionist changed her time automatically.
evidence: the number cannot receive replies.

title: A garden waiting list
text:
The council offers small garden plots to residents who do not have a private garden. Applicants join a waiting list and must renew their interest each January. The council cannot promise how quickly a plot will become available.

Theo applied in March. He received a reference number but no plot offer. In January he missed the renewal email and was removed from the active list. He contacted the office in February, explaining that his address had changed.

The officer found Theo's original application. The policy allowed his position to be restored if he replied within thirty days of removal and confirmed that he still met the eligibility conditions. Theo supplied his new contact details and confirmed that he had no private garden. He was restored to the list, but this did not mean that a plot was immediately available.
question: What does restoration to the list guarantee?
answer: His waiting-list position is restored, not an immediate plot.
wrong: He receives a plot that day.
He never needs to renew his interest again.
evidence: He was restored to the list, but this did not mean that a plot was immediately available.

title: Changing an internet appointment
text:
An internet provider offers installation appointments on weekdays. Customers may change a booking without charge if they give at least two working days' notice. Weekend days do not count towards that notice period.

Ben had a Monday appointment. On Saturday he learned that he would need to work on Monday. He tried to move the installation and expected the change to be free because the appointment was two days away.

The booking team explained that Saturday and Sunday were not working days. Ben could keep the appointment, arrange for another adult to provide access, or pay the late-change fee. He asked his housemate to stay home and checked that the provider accepted access from someone other than the account holder. The team confirmed that it did, provided the adult could show the installer where the equipment should go.
question: Why does Saturday's request not meet the free-change rule?
answer: The rule counts working days, not weekend days.
wrong: Customers cannot change weekday bookings.
Monday is not a working day.
evidence: Weekend days do not count towards that notice period.

title: Sorting waste at an apartment building
text:
The apartment building has separate bins for paper, mixed recycling and general waste. Residents should empty food containers before placing them in mixed recycling. The bins do not accept batteries or electrical appliances.

An inspection found several bags of waste beside the recycling bins. A notice asked residents to place loose recyclable items inside the correct bin and to take batteries to the collection point at the local shop. It also listed the council's collection service for large appliances.

Jules had assumed that any item with a recycling symbol belonged in the building's bins. The caretaker explained that the symbol described the material, while the local service determined which materials could actually be collected. Jules checked the council list before disposing of a broken kettle. He booked the appliance service rather than leaving the kettle beside the bins.
question: Where should Jules arrange disposal of the broken kettle?
answer: Through the council's appliance collection service.
wrong: In the paper bin.
Beside the mixed recycling bin.
evidence: He booked the appliance service rather than leaving the kettle beside the bins.

title: A returned travel claim
text:
The company reimburses travel that is necessary for approved work. Claims must include the purpose of the journey and a receipt. A bank statement can show that money was paid, but it does not always identify what was purchased.

Rina submitted a taxi claim with a bank statement. Finance returned it because the journey and fare were not clearly identified. The company normally expected staff to use public transport, but allowed taxis when equipment could not be carried safely on a bus.

Rina had transported two fragile displays to a client meeting. She obtained an electronic receipt from the taxi company and added a note describing the equipment and meeting. Her manager approved the exception. Finance accepted the revised claim. Rina learned that an exception needed evidence and approval; explaining that the taxi was convenient would not have been sufficient.
question: What supports the exception to the public-transport rule?
answer: The fragile equipment and the manager's approval.
wrong: The taxi was convenient for Rina.
A bank statement removes all other requirements.
evidence: Rina had transported two fragile displays to a client meeting.

title: Joining a swimming class
text:
The leisure centre offers an introductory swimming class for adults. Participants do not need previous swimming experience, but must complete a health declaration before the first session. Class registration and general centre membership are separate.

Luis bought a monthly membership and arrived at the introductory class. Staff explained that his membership allowed access to public swimming sessions, but a place in the taught class required a booking. That day's class was full.

The receptionist put Luis on the class waiting list and gave him the health form. A cancellation became available for the following week, and Luis confirmed that he could attend. The receptionist reminded him to arrive early for the introductory briefing. He could use the public pool in the meantime if he followed the pool's safety guidance, but doing so would not move him ahead on the waiting list.
question: Why could Luis not join the first class immediately?
answer: The class required a separate booking and was full.
wrong: All adult classes require previous swimming experience.
Monthly membership includes every taught class.
evidence: a place in the taught class required a booking. That day's class was full.

title: A new bus route trial
text:
The transport authority is trialling an evening bus route for three months. Buses leave the station at eight and ten on weekdays. The trial will collect information about passenger numbers and connections with late trains.

A newspaper described the route as a permanent new service. The authority published a correction explaining that the timetable would be reviewed after the trial. It invited comments from people who could not use the current departure times, as well as from existing passengers.

Farah worked until nine and could use the ten o'clock bus. Her colleague finished at ten fifteen and still needed a taxi. They sent separate comments describing their shifts. The authority noted that ticket sales alone would not reveal all unmet travel needs. It would consider the comments, operating costs and passenger figures before making a decision.
question: Why does the authority invite comments from non-users?
answer: Ticket sales do not reveal all unmet travel needs.
wrong: The route is already guaranteed permanently.
Passenger numbers will not be collected.
evidence: ticket sales alone would not reveal all unmet travel needs.

title: A job advert with two deadlines
text:
The museum is recruiting seasonal visitor assistants. Applications must arrive by Friday at noon. Shortlisted applicants will be invited to an interview the following Wednesday. A separate deadline applies to requesting reasonable adjustments for the interview.

Alex read the advert quickly and thought that Wednesday was the application deadline. A friend noticed the distinction and encouraged Alex to submit the form before Friday. Alex completed it on Thursday evening.

The application asked for examples of helping visitors and handling unexpected situations. Alex described a time at a community event when directions had changed. The museum later invited Alex to interview and supplied information about the adjustment process. The invitation did not mean that the job had been offered. Alex prepared relevant examples and checked the interview location instead of assuming that recruitment was complete.
question: When must the application arrive?
answer: By Friday at noon.
wrong: On the following Wednesday.
After the interview invitation.
evidence: Applications must arrive by Friday at noon.

title: Replacing a library card
text:
Lost library cards should be reported immediately. The library will suspend the card to prevent further borrowing. Reporting a loss does not remove responsibility for items already borrowed on the account.

Grace lost her card while moving. She reported the loss online and requested a replacement. The system showed that two books were still due the next week. Grace found one at home but could not locate the other.

The librarian explained the difference between replacing a card and resolving a missing book. Grace could renew the loan while searching, if no other reader had reserved the book. If she could not find it, the library would discuss the replacement policy with her. Grace renewed the loan rather than ignoring the notice. Her new card restored access to the same account, including its existing loans.
question: What happens to existing loans when Grace gets a new card?
answer: They remain on the same account.
wrong: They are automatically cancelled.
Only the books she can find remain recorded.
evidence: Her new card restored access to the same account, including its existing loans.

title: A repair cafe and safety limits
text:
The neighbourhood repair cafe helps residents repair everyday objects. Volunteers may show owners how to mend clothes and adjust simple mechanical items. They cannot certify electrical equipment as safe. Owners should check the list of accepted items before attending.

Haruto brought a torn jacket and an electric heater. A volunteer helped him sew the jacket seam. Another volunteer explained that the heater needed a qualified electrical technician. Opening it at the cafe could create a risk that the volunteers were not equipped to assess.

Haruto appreciated the explanation and asked for local repair contacts. The organiser gave him a directory without guaranteeing the work of any listed business. The cafe's goal was to reduce avoidable waste while respecting safety boundaries. It could support some repairs, but the name 'repair cafe' did not mean that every type of damage or equipment could be dealt with there.
question: Why is the heater referred to a qualified technician?
answer: The cafe cannot assess electrical safety adequately.
wrong: Volunteers only repair new clothes.
The directory guarantees every listed repair.
evidence: They cannot certify electrical equipment as safe.

title: A grant application
text:
The council offers small grants for projects that benefit the local community. Applicants must describe the intended participants, budget and expected outcomes. The grant cannot pay for costs incurred before an award is confirmed.

A residents' group wanted to run a free gardening workshop. They submitted an application and bought tools immediately, assuming that their receipt would guarantee repayment. The grants officer explained that the application was still under review.

The group revised its budget to separate the tools already purchased from future costs. It also explained how many residents could attend and how unused materials would be stored. The officer could consider the revised project, but could not promise an award or reimburse the earlier purchase. The group postponed further spending until it received a written decision and checked whether other funding was available for the tools.
question: Which costs cannot be paid by this grant?
answer: Costs incurred before the award is confirmed.
wrong: All future workshop costs.
Costs for projects with local participants.
evidence: The grant cannot pay for costs incurred before an award is confirmed.

title: A course cancellation policy
text:
A language centre refunds course fees when a student withdraws at least seven days before the course starts. Later withdrawals may receive credit for a future course, but cash refunds are not normally available. The policy lists exceptions for documented emergencies.

Eva changed jobs three days before her course began. Her new shifts conflicted with the lessons. She asked for a refund and explained the change in her timetable.

The administrator offered credit towards an evening course later in the year. Eva checked the available dates and the expiry of the credit. She also asked whether the centre could move her to an online class immediately. There was a place, but she needed suitable equipment and a reliable connection. Eva chose the later evening course. She received confirmation stating its date, price and the credit applied, so the new arrangement was clear.
question: What is normally available for a late withdrawal?
answer: Credit for a future course.
wrong: An automatic cash refund in every case.
No possible alternative arrangement.
evidence: Later withdrawals may receive credit for a future course, but cash refunds are not normally available.

title: Sharing office space
text:
A shared office has quiet desks, a discussion area and two small rooms for calls. Call rooms may be booked for thirty minutes at a time. Regular membership does not include a permanent private office.

Mateo made a long client call at a quiet desk. Another member asked him to use a call room. Both rooms were occupied, so Mateo argued that the desk should be available for any kind of work.

The manager pointed out that members had agreed to separate quiet work from conversations. Mateo could use the discussion area for a non-confidential call or wait for a room. Because the call involved private information, he asked the client to speak later. The manager reviewed booking demand and considered adding another room. That possible improvement did not remove the current quiet-area rule.
question: Why does Mateo postpone the call?
answer: It involves private information and no call room is free.
wrong: Membership gives him a permanent office.
All calls are prohibited everywhere.
evidence: Because the call involved private information, he asked the client to speak later.

title: Booking a train with a bicycle
text:
The regional train accepts bicycles on selected services. A passenger ticket and a bicycle reservation are separate. Bicycle spaces are limited, and a ticket does not guarantee a space. Folding bicycles may be carried as luggage if they meet the stated size limits.

Chloe bought a ticket for a morning train and later tried to reserve a bicycle space. The spaces were already full. She considered arriving early, but the operator explained that reserved spaces could not be replaced by a queue at the station.

Chloe could choose a later service with available space, use a qualifying folding bicycle, or travel without her bicycle. She changed to the later train and checked whether the fare difference applied. The revised confirmation listed both her seat and bicycle reservation. She saved both details so that she could show them separately if required.
question: Why does arriving early not solve Chloe's problem?
answer: The limited bicycle spaces are already reserved.
wrong: Every bicycle is treated as ordinary luggage.
A passenger ticket guarantees bicycle space.
evidence: reserved spaces could not be replaced by a queue at the station.

title: A food label and a delivery complaint
text:
The meal delivery service asks customers to report missing or damaged items within twenty-four hours. Photographs help staff identify packaging problems. The service also asks customers to check storage instructions when food arrives.

Imani received a box that had been left at the wrong entrance. She found it later in the afternoon. A cold item was no longer at the temperature recommended on its label. She photographed the box and contacted customer support instead of tasting the item to judge safety.

Support recorded both the delivery error and the storage concern. It arranged a replacement and reminded the courier of the correct entrance. Imani's complaint included the delivery time, collection time and label instructions. That evidence helped staff understand the sequence; saying only that the meal was disappointing would not have shown which part of the service had failed.
question: What helps staff understand the complaint's sequence?
answer: The delivery time, collection time and label instructions.
wrong: Only a general statement that the meal was disappointing.
Tasting the item to test its safety.
evidence: Imani's complaint included the delivery time, collection time and label instructions.

title: An employee training agreement
text:
The company pays tuition for approved work-related courses. Staff should obtain approval before enrolling. Travel and examination fees are considered separately, and an agreement must say which costs are covered.

Wei received permission to attend a technical course. The initial email approved tuition only. He later submitted an examination fee, believing that completing the course necessarily included the exam. Finance asked him to check the agreement.

His manager agreed that the examination was relevant and submitted a separate request for approval. The request could be considered, but the original tuition approval did not guarantee payment. Wei waited for the written decision before booking the examination. For future courses, he planned to ask about tuition, materials, travel and examination charges at the beginning, rather than treating all related costs as one item.
question: What did the initial approval cover?
answer: Tuition only.
wrong: Every cost related to the course.
The examination fee only.
evidence: The initial email approved tuition only.

title: A housing inspection
text:
The landlord must arrange access with tenants before a routine inspection. Tenants may propose an alternative reasonable time if the suggested appointment is unsuitable. Emergency access is governed by a different procedure.

Sofia received a notice for a Thursday morning inspection. She would be working away from home that day. She replied promptly, offering Friday morning or Monday afternoon. The landlord agreed to Friday and sent a confirmation.

Sofia also reported a recurring window leak and attached photographs taken after rain. The landlord added the problem to the inspection notes but explained that identifying the cause might require a later specialist visit. Sofia understood that arranging access was an immediate step, while confirming the repair was a separate decision. She kept the appointment confirmation and photographs so that both parties had a clear record.
question: What does Friday's confirmation establish?
answer: The agreed inspection time, not a completed repair.
wrong: That the leak has already been repaired.
That emergency access rules apply to every inspection.
evidence: identifying the cause might require a later specialist visit.

title: A public survey
text:
The council is asking residents about proposed changes to a town-centre square. The survey explains three options and their estimated costs. It also includes a space for comments about needs that the options may not address.

A social media post claimed that the option with the most survey votes would automatically be built. The council clarified that the survey was one source of evidence. Accessibility, maintenance costs and legal requirements would also be considered.

Noah preferred more seating but noticed that one drawing left little space for wheelchair access. He described this concern in his comment instead of choosing an option without qualification. The council published a summary separating support for each option from recurring concerns. It had not yet made a final decision. The summary explained what the survey showed and which questions still required further work.
question: How will survey votes be used?
answer: As one source of evidence alongside other requirements.
wrong: As an automatic final construction decision.
Only comments, never votes, will be considered.
evidence: The council clarified that the survey was one source of evidence.

title: A scholarship condition
text:
The adult education scholarship covers half the tuition for eligible residents on approved courses. Applicants must provide evidence of residence and income. The scholarship does not pay for equipment, travel or optional activities.

Dylan read a headline offering support for adult learners. He assumed that his camera and travel costs would be included. The application guide explained the narrower coverage and the evidence required.

Dylan checked whether his photography course was approved and calculated the remaining costs. He could borrow equipment from the provider, but needed to reserve it separately. He submitted the scholarship application with the required documents and waited for a decision. Eligibility to apply did not mean that funding was already awarded. Dylan planned an affordable alternative in case his application was unsuccessful, rather than enrolling on the basis of the headline alone.
question: What does eligibility to apply mean here?
answer: The application can be considered, but funding is not yet awarded.
wrong: Equipment and travel are automatically funded.
Half of every applicant's costs are guaranteed.
evidence: Eligibility to apply did not mean that funding was already awarded.

title: Preparing a community event
text:
The neighbourhood association planned a Saturday event with talks, food and a small exhibition. Its budget included room hire, printing and refreshments. The organiser checked access times because the hired room was available from nine, while visitors were invited for ten.

Two volunteers expected to set up on Friday evening. The venue explained that the previous night's booking made this impossible. The group changed the exhibition layout so that it could be assembled quickly on Saturday.

The organiser sent a final checklist naming who would bring each item, when they should arrive and where supplies would be stored. Volunteers confirmed their tasks rather than replying only that the plan looked good. After the event, the group compared the checklist with what actually happened. It recorded one late delivery and suggested an earlier confirmation call next time. The review identified a practical change without assuming that one successful event proved every future plan would work.
question: Why does the group simplify the exhibition layout?
answer: They cannot set up on Friday evening.
wrong: The room is available all Friday night.
Visitors will arrive before the hire begins.
evidence: The venue explained that the previous night's booking made this impossible.
